_comment: What this application considers mandatory before it can be used.
One file, read by two consumers: the first-launch bootstrap in
desktop/bootstrap/ and the running server through
src/server/setup-manifest.ts. That is the point — a required model named in
two places is a required model that will eventually disagree with itself,
and the version that loses is always the one a user is looking at.
JSON rather than a module because the bootstrap reads it with the bundled
Node runtime while the server has it inlined by the bundler, and JSON is
the one format both of those do without ceremony.
Bump `revision` only when a release genuinely needs an installed component
to change. It re-runs provisioning for every existing installation.

runtime._comment: Node ships with the application. Python is optional: without it the design catalogue falls back to the application's own rules, exactly as on a server without Python.

skills.label: UI/UX Pro Max
skills._comment: Every file the design-system path actually opens. A directory existing proves nothing: an interrupted npm install leaves one behind with half its catalogue.

verify._comment: The same call the generator makes, so 'verified' means the application can use it rather than that its files exist.

ai._comment: requiredModel is THE model identifier for this application. WG_OLLAMA_MODEL overrides it for an operator who has a reason; nothing else may name a default.

installer._comment: Ollama publishes no stable per-release digest at this URL, so integrity is enforced by what can be checked: the bytes received must match the declared length, the file must be a real Windows executable, and it must be a plausible size. WG_OLLAMA_SETUP_SHA256 pins an exact digest when an operator has one.

application._comment: Created before anything else, so a later step never fails on a missing parent directory.

_comment: Setup may only report itself complete when every component below is
accounted for.
mandatory: must have verified. A failure here leaves setup incomplete and
the next launch resumes it — the application does not open pretending to
be ready.
optionalWithConsent: must have verified, OR the user must have been shown
the failure and have chosen to continue without it. That choice is
recorded as `skipped`. The application genuinely generates websites with
no local model, so trapping someone in a setup screen over one would be
worse than starting — but it is never decided on their behalf and never
silently.

disk._comment: The whole first launch, not just the model. Ollama installs about 4.5 GB of runtime and CUDA libraries from a 700 MB download, the installer is written to a temporary file first, and a machine left with nothing free is a machine that cannot write its own database.
